Name: Establishing an outreach, inspection, and enforcement plan for reducing the fire risks posed by certain powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries used by such devices.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing an outreach, inspection, and enforcement plan for reducing the fire risks posed by certain powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries used by such devices
BodyName: Committee on Fire and Emergency Management

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Fire and Emergency Management

Summary: This legislation would require the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) and the Fire Department (FDNY) develop and implement a targeted outreach, inspection and enforcement plan to mitigate the risk of death, injury and property damage resulting from fires caused by certain powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries used by such devices. The goal of such plan would be to: (i) reduce the sale, use, and possession of products that do not meet safety standards established by local law; and (ii) ensure that devices and storage batteries are stored and charged in a manner consistent with relevant fire code requirements.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing an outreach, inspection, and enforcement plan for reducing the fire risks posed by certain powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries used by such devices  

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:
Section 1. Subchapter 2 of chapter 4 of title 20 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 20-610.2 to read as follows:
§ 20-610.2. Targeted outreach, inspection, and enforcement. a. No later than March 1, 2027, the department, in consultation with the fire department and any other agency designated by the mayor, shall develop and implement a targeted outreach, inspection and enforcement plan to mitigate the risk of death, injury and property damage resulting from fires caused by certain powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries used by such devices. Such plan shall include specific inspection, outreach and enforcement policies and protocols of each relevant agency designed to: (i) reduce the sale, use, and possession of products that do not meet the safety standards established by sections 609 and 610 of this subchapter; and (ii) ensure that devices and storage batteries are stored and charged in a manner consistent with relevant fire code requirements. 
b.  The plan developed pursuant to subdivision b of this section shall include, but need not be limited to: 
1. Risk-based inspection and enforcement initiatives that prioritize locations, businesses, and sellers identified through analysis of: (i) prior violations issued for related local law and fire code provisions; (ii) complaints received by city agencies or the city’s 311 customer service center; (iii) fire incident data, including the geographic locations and occupancy and business types where fire incidents have been determined to have been caused by a powered bicycle, powered mobility device, or storage battery used by such device; and (iv) businesses types that present elevated fire risks due to the nature of operations, or the presence and use of powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries for such devices for commercial purposes. 
2. Strategies for identifying and addressing online and remote distribution, sale, lease, or rental of devices and storage batteries that do not meet local safety standards, including through enforcement actions and legal proceedings against persons and entities engaging in commercial activity on online marketplaces, social media platforms, and other remote means, in violation of local law. 
3. Strategies for identifying and addressing the possession and use of devices and storage batteries that do not meet local safety standards for sale, including through targeted outreach, inspection, and enforcement of businesses that use powered bicycles, or powered mobility devices, for commercial purposes.
4. Strategies for education and outreach to retailers, repair shops, delivery workers, employers, building owners, and residents, regarding certification requirements, safe charging and storage, and the hazards of using devices and storage batteries that do not meet local safety standards.
5. Enforcement protocols and policies that establish when agencies will issue violations, or when authorized by law, seize or remove products from commercial or residential locations, or seal the premises of commercial entities, for repeated violations of related local laws.
c. The plan developed pursuant to subdivision b of this section shall be submitted to the mayor and speaker of the city council, published on the department’s website, and updated annually. 
§ 2. Subchapter 2 of chapter 4 of title 20 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 20-610.3 to read as follows:
§ 20-610.3. Reporting.  No later than April 1, 2027, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department, in consultation with the fire department and any other agency designated by the mayor, shall report on agency inspections and enforcement, related to local safety standards for powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries, and the occurrence of fire incidents caused by such devices and storage batteries. Such report shall include, but need not be limited to the following for the prior quarter: 
a. A list of all fire incidents that occurred during the prior quarter in which the fire department identified a powered bicycle, powered mobility device, or storage battery for such device, as the suspected or confirmed cause of such fire, including: 1. the geographic location and building occupancy type where each such fire occurred; and 2. whether circumstances at each such incident indicated compliance with relevant fire code and administrative code provisions, provided that such information can be ascertained; and 3. identification of all related local law or fire code provisions not met at such location.  The fire department shall periodically update information from prior quarterly reports upon completion of any related fire marshal investigations confirming the causes of such fires.  
b. Performance metrics to evaluate the city’s implementation of the plan created pursuant to section 610.2 of this subchapter, including, but not limited to, the following information for each related inspection or enforcement action taken by the city during the prior quarter: 1. the date of such inspection or enforcement action; 2. the geographic location, occupancy type, and where applicable, business type, of such inspection or enforcement action; 3. the agency conducting such inspection or enforcement action; 4. number of violations issued disaggregated by local law or fire code provision; 5. the number powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, or storage batteries used for such devices, seized or removed during such action; and 6. whether the business or location had been subject to related city inspection within the prior 6-months, and whether any violations had  been issued at such location or against such business during the prior 2-years. 
§3. This local law takes effect immediately.
